stories.headline: UAE Oil Tanker Attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Iran Outlines Conditions to Reopen Waterway
stories.body: An oil tanker owned by Abu Dhabi state-owned energy firm Adnoc was hit by an Iranian missile in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday [c6]. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that a vessel east of Khasab, Oman, caught fire after being struck by a projectile [c8]. Following the attack, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs characterized the missile strike on the Adnoc vessel as an act of piracy by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [c14]. Statements condemning the missile strike were quickly issued by Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, and the Gulf Cooperation Council [c15]. This strike highlights the physical danger that tanker sailors continue to face while transiting the Strait of Hormuz as of August 2026 [c1]. Adnoc stated that more than a dozen of its vessels have been targeted by missile and drone attacks in the waterway since February 2026, leaving one person dead and 20 injured [c7]. The ongoing unrest poses severe risks to global energy security, as approximately one-fifth of global oil and natural gas supplies normally pass through the Strait of Hormuz [c9]. Tensions in the region remain elevated further south as well, where Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis imposed a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports in the Red Sea starting on July 20 [c10]. Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States changes its military and political conduct [c2]. Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who serves as the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and is a commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, outlined Tehran's stance [c3]. Iran's explicit demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz include the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, full compensation for war damage, and the unconditional release of frozen assets [c4]. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz will certainly reopen whenever the United States accepts Tehran's conditions [c12]. Despite the standoff, some communication and partial transit continue. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran and Oman were close to agreeing on a transit route through the Strait of Hormuz [c5]. Araghchi also stated that maritime traffic had restored to 60 percent of normal levels within two weeks of implementing Clause 5 of the June Memorandum of Understanding [c13]. In addition, US Vice President JD Vance told Fox News that Iran informed Washington it has no intentions to charge tolls on ships in the Strait of Hormuz [c11].

vocab.meaning: the act of passing through or across a place
connected with the sea, navigation, or shipping
an object thrown or fired forward as a weapon

stories.headline: Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella Takes Office Promising Anti-Terror Campaign
stories.body: Abelardo de la Espriella has taken office as President of Colombia after defeating leftist candidate Ivan Cepeda in June's run-off election by less than 1 percent of the vote [c18]. De la Espriella, a former defence lawyer who represented drug-trafficking paramilitary figures [c23] and nicknames himself 'The Tiger' [c24], broke with tradition by holding his presidential inauguration ceremony in Cali instead of the capital city of Bogota [c21]. Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche headed the official United States delegation at the event [c27]. In his maiden speech at a military base in Cali, President de la Espriella vowed to defeat narco-terrorists [c24]. He announced plans to join the US-led 'Shield of the Americas' security partnership [c22] and resume aerial spraying of herbicides to eradicate illicit coca crops [c26]. Following his swearing-in, the US State Department pledged $1 billion in security assistance to Colombia [c20]. Espriella also campaigned on promises to reduce the size of the Colombian state by up to 40 percent [c25]. Internationally, he plans to restore diplomatic relations with Israel while cutting ties with Cuba and Nicaragua [c29]. Outgoing President Gustavo Petro, who pursued a 'Total Peace' strategy starting in 2022 emphasizing dialogue with criminal and rebel groups [c19], refused to attend the inauguration and called for mass public protests over unproven election fraud allegations [c28]. Violence persisted nearby as a car bomb attributed by the military to two FARC dissident factions exploded at a Pan-American Highway toll plaza in Cauca, injuring two security guards [c16, c17].

vocab.meaning: a formal ceremony marking the beginning of a leader's term
disagreeing with an established religious or political system
a chemical substance used to destroy unwanted plants or crops

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey Sign Mutual Defence Pact in Mecca
stories.body: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed a trilateral mutual defence agreement during a meeting in Mecca on Friday [c30]. The joint statement stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three member nations will be considered an attack against all three [c31]. A Turkish official stated that the agreement is purely defensive and does not replace existing security commitments [c35]. Turkey maintains the second-largest standing military force within the 32-member NATO alliance [c33]. Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif advocated expanding the pact into a broader NATO-like military alliance for Islamic nations [c34]. The agreement expands existing bilateral ties. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan previously established a bilateral mutual defence agreement containing a similar collective defence clause in September 2025 [c32]. Historically, Pakistan has stationed military personnel, fighter aircraft, and air-defence systems inside Saudi Arabia [c37]. Turkey also provided military support, including uncrewed aerial vehicles and electronic warfare equipment, to Pakistan during India's Operation Sindoor in May 2025 [c36]. The announcement of the pact coincided with a new military offensive by Yemen's Saudi-backed government against the Houthis [c38].

vocab.meaning: an aggressive military attack or campaign

stories.headline: US Senate Confirms Former Trump Lawyer Todd Blanche as Attorney General
stories.body: The US Senate confirmed former Trump defense lawyer Todd Blanche as US Attorney General by a 50-49 vote [c39]. Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana provided the deciding 50th vote [c44]. Republican Senators Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski joined all Senate Democrats in voting against Blanche [c41]. Following the vote, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer accused Republicans on X of handing President Trump an excuse to continue widespread corruption [c40]. Conversely, Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley commended Blanche on X for displaying patience, compassion, and tenacity [c46]. Blanche represented Donald Trump as his private defence attorney in criminal proceedings prior to joining the Department of Justice [c47]. He was appointed acting Attorney General in April 2026 after President Trump dismissed former Attorney General Pam Bondi [c48]. During confirmation proceedings, Blanche pledged to abandon a proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponisation compensation fund [c45]. He also adjusted an agreement granting tax audit immunity to Donald Trump and his sons so that it applies retroactively rather than to future tax filings [c49]. The confirmation vote took place as the Senate passed a resolution confirming a slate of 71 Trump administration nominees before entering a five-week recess [c42], including former campaign operative P. Wells Griffith as US Ambassador to the International Atomic Energy Agency in Vienna [c43].

vocab.meaning: a temporary pause or break in official work or proceedings
the quality of being persistent and determined
applying to events or actions that occurred in the past

stories.headline: Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv Region as Zelensky Warns of Winter Energy Crisis
stories.body: Russian forces launched a renewed overnight barrage of missiles and drones targeting the capital city of Kyiv and surrounding areas early Saturday morning [c59]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that overnight Russian missile strikes and frontline shelling killed 13 people across Ukraine over a 24-hour period [c51]. Among the casualties, a three-year-old child was killed and four family members and neighbours were injured during a Russian strike on a village in the Kyiv region [c52]. Speaking in Belgrade, President Zelensky stated that Ukraine faces an upcoming winter with virtually no working thermal power plants remaining [c50]. He urged foreign nations to enforce stricter sanctions to prevent international components from reaching Russia's missile manufacturing supply chains [c54]. Meanwhile, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic stated during a joint press conference that Serbia has not discussed military cooperation with Ukraine and maintains its policy of not imposing sanctions on Russia [c53]. In response to ongoing Russian aggression, Ukraine conducts near-daily long-range drone attacks against Russian oil facilities to disrupt fuel supplies used to fund Russia's military operations [c58]. The Ukrainian Armed Forces launched overnight drone strikes targeting Russia's Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries, causing fires at both facilities [c55]. In a separate incident, a Maya decoy drone model used by Ukraine entered Bulgarian airspace from Romania and detonated near an international gas pipeline without causing injuries, according to the Bulgarian Defence Ministry [c56, c57].

vocab.meaning: a heavy and concentrated outpouring of missile or artillery fire
an imitation device used to trick or distract an enemy

stories.headline: US Senate Passes Bill Imposing 100% Tariffs on Key Russian Oil Buyers Including India
stories.body: The United States Senate has approved a major trade bill aimed at penalizing countries that purchase Russian crude oil, passing the Lindsey Graham-named bill in an 86-11 vote [c65]. The legislation authorizes tariffs of up to 500 percent on Russian imports, as well as 100 percent tariffs on five key Russian oil buyers, including India and China [c65]. However, the measure will not take effect immediately, as the House of Representatives is not expected to consider the Senate-passed tariff legislation until September following its summer recess [c66]. The legislative move comes after a period of fluctuating economic measures and negotiations between Washington and New Delhi. The United States previously raised overall tariff rates on Indian goods to 50 percent in August 2025 due to India's continued imports of Russian crude oil [c63]. In February, President Donald Trump issued an executive order removing a 25 percent punitive tariff on Indian goods after reaching an interim trade agreement with New Delhi [c67]. Later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump met in France in June 2026, where they instructed officials to negotiate a bilateral trade agreement [c62]. Diplomatic dialogue between the two nations has continued alongside the legislative actions in Washington. US Vice President JD Vance placed a phone call to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation across key sectors including trade, defence, energy, and technology [c60]. During the conversation, Prime Minister Modi extended personal congratulations to JD Vance and Second Lady Usha Vance following the birth of their son [c61]. Vice President JD Vance and Usha Vance announced the birth of their fourth child, Alec Neel Vance, making him the first child born to a sitting US Vice President in over 150 years [c64].

vocab.meaning: a duty or tax placed by a government on imported goods
temporary or intended to cover a short intervening period

stories.headline: Political Row Erupts in India Over Women's Reservation and Seat Delimitation Links
stories.body: A political debate has erupted between Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi on X regarding the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill [c68]. Rahul Gandhi urged Minister Rijiju to implement the 2023 Women's Reservation Law immediately without linking it to constituency delimitation [c69]. The central government's proposed delimitation agenda seeks to increase the maximum capacity of the Lok Sabha from 550 seats to 850 seats [c79]. Meanwhile, Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at his Parliament House office on Friday, August 7, 2026 [c70]. Badal reversed his party's previous opposition, endorsing the rollout of 33 percent women's reservation alongside a proposed 50 percent expansion of Lok Sabha seats in 2029 [c78]. The Shiromani Akali Dal had previously withdrawn from the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance coalition in 2020 over disputed central agricultural laws [c71]. In Tamil Nadu, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay hosted a conference of state MPs to formulate opposition to the Centre's delimitation plan [c72]. Around 21 MPs representing parties including Congress, VCK, CPI, CPI(M), MDMK, and IUML attended [c73]. However, major regional parties DMK and AIADMK abstained [c74], leading to 37 out of 57 total Tamil Nadu MPs boycotting the meeting [c76]. Congress MP Karti Chidambaram stated that Tamil Nadu's political representation in Parliament must be preserved at 39 members out of a frozen total strength of 543 seats [c75], while Congress MP Praveen Chakraborty expressed disappointment over DMK and AIADMK boycotting the meeting called to defend state representation rights [c77].

vocab.meaning: the fixing or adjusting of boundaries or seat allocations
to choose not to consume something or not to take part in an action
